text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- A dispatch signed by the Under Secretary for Labour yesterday said breaks during working hours were effective work, as long as the worker is close to his work station.
- This week parliament will approve a diploma making public competitions compulsory for senior civil service jobs.

- Forty-nine out of the 70 UNITA MPs, who have waited four years to join parliament, arrived at Luanda. The U.N. representative and UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi will discuss the launch of the Government for Unity and National Reconciliation.

- The Economy Ministry plans to sign an authorisation to allow German group Siemens, U.S. carmakers Ford and General Motors, the Halla Group of South Korea and UTA of the United States to invest a total of 50 billion escudos in several projects, creating some 3,000 new jobs.
- The Farmers' Association has disputed a list prepared by the Agriculture Ministry naming beneficiaries of European Union agricultural aid.
- Construction investment rose sharply and purchasing power improved, the National Statistics Institute (INE) said in a February report.

- An agreement between the government and the pharmaceutical industry foresees increases in prices of medicines in 1998 and 1999 of below the inflation rate. This year prices of medicines will be frozen.

- The government and textiles companies will sign an agreement in the northern city of Guimaraes today as a first step to guarantee that companies will fully respect laws to protect the environment by 1999.
- The government plans to boost the social security fund by between 50 and 60 billion escudos, which will mean it will have to present a supplementary budget to parliament.
